chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Udhiyah (sacrifice) in Mina, so he said: 'Four days.' And about the Udhiyah in other towns, so he said: 'Three days.'

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or Eid al-Adha
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina (a specific location near Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the duration for offering Udhiyah in Mina versus other towns according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal scope of the Udhiyah sacrifice, distinguishing the four-day period in Mina (including the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah plus the day of Eid) from the three-day period applicable elsewhere. It reflects the scholarly consensus on the practical application of Quranic injunctions regarding Hajj rituals, ensuring pilgrims adhere to the specific legal windows for fulfilling this Sunnah.
